subject: 🏃 Monday — Hip Complex Circuit / Deload Begins (Wk 8)
html:
Tomorrow you have the Monday Hip Complex Circuit — 20 minutes of mobility, nothing more. This is the first day of Week 8, the deload week, and it's the day after the Presidio Half Marathon. Your body just raced 13.1 miles on a hilly bridge course at a suffer score of 235 — the highest of the entire V6 plan. The only job tomorrow is recovery.

The circuit: 90/90 switches, adductor rockbacks, foam rolling (quads, IT band, calves), plus the PT mobility flush — foam roller T-spine extensions, standing lunges with hip IR + extension, and quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side). Two rounds, ~20 min total. Move slowly through the positions. If anything is stiff or tender from yesterday's race, spend extra time there — this is diagnostic, not a workout.

Focus cue: listen to the post-race body. Note how the quads and calves feel after yesterday's 555 ft of climbing and the bridge descents. Any residual knee awareness gets logged — yesterday was 1/5 crossing the line, but the eccentric descent load from the Golden Gate out-and-back can announce itself 24–48 hours later. If the knee talks tomorrow, that's terrain-load feedback, not a flare — but log it so we track it.

Where you are: Week 8 of 12, Phase 2 deload. The Presidio pivot test is in the books — verdict: hold 3:30 (2 of 3 gates passed; time gate missed by ~35–50 s, but the fitness landed right on the 3:25 break-even line). Knee passed clean, HR passed clean. The binding constraint exposed yesterday isn't the engine — it's fueling at race effort (one gel in 97 minutes). That's the #1 project for the back half of the build, and we start solving it this week. The deload runs Tue–Sun (4 mi easy, low-volume strength, 6 mi easy, 10 mi long run) — all recovery-paced, no quality work. Let the legs come back.

Tonight: Hydrate well, eat a solid recovery dinner (protein + carbs to restock — fish, rice, roasted veg), and get to bed early. No alarm pressure tomorrow — the circuit can happen any time. Good race yesterday. Now recover.
